newsitem.title: USA: Commercial spy satellites to be launched soon - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Commercial spy satellites to be launched soon - NYT.

text.p: The first commercial spy satellite is scheduled to be launched in April or May, ending the monopoly on orbital espionage held by the governments of advanced nations, the New York Times said Monday.
Earthwatch, whose corporate partners include Ball Corp's aerospace and technologies group and Hitachi Ltd, is planning to launch its satellite from Siberia atop a Russian rocket, the paper said.
The report said another satellite will fly into orbit in December, followed by as many as a dozen in the next decade.
Other companies involved in the fledging field are Eastman Kodak and Space Imaging Inc, a private company in Thornton, Colorado, owned by Lockheed Martin and Raytheon's E-Systems Inc.
Also pursuing the work are Boeing Co, Motorola Inc and the Orbital Sciences Corp of Dulles, Virginia, the paper said.

The Times said the satellites enable anyone with a credit card to see objects on the ground as small as cars and hot tubs and peer into the compounds of dictators as well as the yards of next-door neighbors.

Companies involved are eagerly touting the technology's mass appeal as a source of travel information and as a tool in law enforcement, disaster relief and urban planning while playing down thorny questions of privacy, the report said.
